title: Single-coefficient section-normalized open restriction comparison
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E/Q_l, an arbitrary open immersion j:X→Z, section-normalized slice operations o [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison], and n≥0. The finite slice restriction functor has a unique natural isomorphism r to intrinsic open restriction [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-adjunction] satisfying SfFiniteOpenRestrictionNormalized. Precisely, evaluate on a slice object V and on any section of the fixed-scalar inverse realization of an ambient module N. Carry that section to N using the actual realization unit and counit and recompose the slice object via its canonical isomorphism to V.left. Carry it through the inverse of the slice-equivalence counit, then apply o.finite.functor to r and identify its forward functor by o.finiteFunctor. The result equals the realization-unit section of the fixed-scalar restriction at sliceSite(V). There is no adjacent coefficient comparison or extension comparison in this assertion.

proof.text: Restrict intrinsic modules to the constant scalar presheaf. The module sheafification adjunction is fully faithful on its right adjoint. On a fixed-scalar sheaf its unit is invertible, because the underlying abelian presheaf is already a sheaf. Compose this unit with the actual realization counit to obtain fixedSectionIso, whose section functions are exactly sfFixedToIntrinsicSection and are bijective.

Whisker the ambient constant-scalar unit with the slice forgetful functor. Cocontinuity preserves its local bijectivity, so restriction to these constant scalars on the slice is fully faithful as well. The canonical sfFiniteOpenSliceObjectIso gives a natural recomposition isomorphism of fixed-scalar section diagrams. The equation o.finiteConstants supplies the scalar square for the concrete pushforward: after restriction to constants its comparison is the identity on sections. Use o.finiteFunctor to identify this pushforward with the supplied equivalence functor.

Compose the inverse ambient fixedSectionIso, slice recomposition and open realization unit. Cancel the fully faithful slice constant-scalar restriction to obtain an intrinsic slice comparison. Precompose it with the supplied slice-equivalence counit and cancel that equivalence functor to construct r. Its normalization follows from naturality of fixedSectionIso, the inverse identities of the slice-object isomorphism, and the slice-equivalence counit. For uniqueness cancel the faithful equivalence functor, its invertible counit and the finiteFunctor identification; the required maps agree on every section since the fixedSectionIso and slice-object section maps are surjective. No quasi-compactness assumption is used.

The retained left-comparison definition is the unique left-adjoint isomorphism obtained from the composite finite slice adjunction after transporting its right adjoint along the supplied r, and the intrinsic extension-by-zero adjunction.

theorem sfFiniteOpenRestriction_presentation (n : ℕ) :
    ∃! r : IntegralOpenReduction.finiteRestriction l E j o n ≅
        sfIntrinsicOpenRestriction j (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)),
      SfFiniteOpenRestrictionNormalized l E j o n r
